svg.title: A nurse is planning to collect a specimen from a male infant using a urine collection bag. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
svg.desc: The bag is adhesive , so the skin has to be clean and completely dry for it to seal — a damp or greasy perineum means the specimen leaks into the diaper. Lubricant does exactly what the nurse is trying to avoid: no oil, lotion, powder or lubricant goes anywhere near the skin. In a boy the penis and the scrotum both go inside the bag , with the adhesive started at the bridge of skin between the anus and the scrotum. And the bag is checked every 20–30 minutes and removed as soon as the infant voids — waiting hours contaminates the sample and macerates the skin. Remember a bagged specimen is not sterile: it is acceptable for a urinalysis , but a culture needs a catheterized specimen.
